items.heading: Seemantham / Godh Bharai-type ceremonies
details: Bring family and community together around a pregnancy, providing meaningful social support.

items.heading: Traditional postpartum family support
details: Extended family help reduces household workload for the mother during recovery.

items.heading: Traditional postpartum nutritious foods
details: Specially prepared foods can provide extra energy, protein, and micronutrients during recovery.

items.heading: Colostrum feeding
details: The first breast milk provides concentrated antibodies and immune factors to the newborn.

items.heading: Skin-to-skin contact
details: Supports a newborn's temperature regulation, physiological stability, and early bonding.

items.heading: Traditional baby massage
details: Gentle, regular massage can promote relaxation and strengthen the bond between parent and infant.

items.heading: Postpartum oil massage
details: Can provide relaxation and muscle comfort for the mother during recovery.

items.heading: Applying kajal on babies
details: Traditionally made from soot or herbs, kajal was believed to protect an infant's eyes from harsh sunlight and dust.
A small dot on a baby's cheek or forehead was also a folk custom believed to "ward off the evil eye."

items.heading: Shaving a baby's first hair (Mundan)
details: Removing the fine birth hair was traditionally believed to encourage stronger, healthier hair growth later.
Briefly exposing the scalp to gentle sunlight was thought to aid the infant's vitamin D absorption.
